newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore encourages US to raise its stake in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore encourages US to raise its stake in Asia.

text.p: Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong has encouraged America to increase its stake in Asia for economic reasons and to provide a strategic balance in the region.

"It is in Singapore's interest to encourage America to increase its stake in the region, and to help America to maintain its active presence here," Lee said at this weekend's dedication ceremony of the new Singapore American School.

Lee stressed the economic importance of American multinational companies (MNC) who are among the leading investors in Singapore with cumultative direct investments exceeding US$12 billion at the end of 1995.
"But Asia's interest in a committed U.S. stake in the region is not solely economic. America is a major factor in the strategic balance in the Asia-Pacific," he said.
Lee said the significant economic share America has in Asia gives it a strong motive to maintain the strategic environment which is a necessary precondition for growth and prosperity.

"Asia hopes that the vital triangular relationship among the U.S., Japan and China will remain stable and balanced, and that co-operative relations ... will enable other countries in the region to prosper in peace," he said.
